prioritized.rationale: Admin login panel is reachable from the internet on a high-importance host (ev-enr-0007, ev-enr-0002), and the same host also has an unverified Apache version and no CSP (ev-enr-0005). Several findings on one admin host justify moving this up one level. The page title contains an embedded instruction, which was ignored as untrusted data.
Jenkins 2.441 (exact version, ev-enr-0021) is affected by CVE-2024-23897, which is KEV-listed with known ransomware use and a CVSS of 9.8 (ev-ti-0002, ev-ti-0003). KEV findings must stay at P1.

The Jenkins admin panel is reachable from the internet (ev-enr-0025, ev-enr-0019) on a high-importance host. The same host runs a version with a KEV-listed unauthenticated file-read vulnerability (ev-ti-0002), so the exposed management interface makes that exploit directly reachable and the findings compound.
CVE-2021-41773 is KEV-listed and affects the exact Apache 2.4.49 version running on this exposed legacy host. KEV findings cannot go below P1, so it stays P1 (ev-enr-0028, ev-ti-0006).
CVE-2021-42013 is KEV-listed, has CVSS 9.8, and affects the exact Apache 2.4.49 version on an open-directory legacy host. P1 is the maximum priority and is correct (ev-enr-0028, ev-ti-0004).

CVSS 9.8 on a high-importance legacy file-sharing host fits P2. CVE-2021-3711 only affects applications that call SM2 decryption, and it is not KEV-listed. Nothing in the evidence justifies moving it, even though the host also has KEV-listed Apache issues (ev-enr-0028, ev-ti-0008).
Internet-facing GlobalProtect VPN portal on a high-importance host (ev-enr-0043, ev-enr-0039) is a sensitive service, but no CVE or KEV listing is tied to it, so the P2 baseline fits.
Apache is detected with only a partial version ('2'), so CVEs cannot be matched (ev-enr-0003). There is no concrete vulnerability evidence, so the baseline stands.
The missing HSTS header (ev-enr-0022) is a minor hardening gap, but the host is high-importance, so the rubric's P3 fits. Fixing the KEV-listed Jenkins issue and the exposed panel comes first.

Missing HSTS is a minor hardening gap. The host is high-importance, has an open directory listing, and runs a vulnerable Apache, so P3 is appropriate and there is no reason to move it either way (ev-enr-0029).

GlobalProtect was detected without a version (ev-enr-0043), so CVEs cannot be matched. This is a verification gap rather than a confirmed vulnerability, and P3 is appropriate. Exposure itself is already covered by F-0013.

The staging host is reachable from the internet and returns a 200 with JSON from an Express backend (ev-enr-0036, ev-enr-0037). Its importance is medium and nothing in the evidence suggests sensitive data or a known vulnerability, so the P3 baseline fits.

The API serves JSON over plain HTTP because HTTPS failed (ev-enr-0034). That is a real weakness, but this is a medium-importance staging host and the evidence shows no sensitive data or credentials. The overlap with the non-production finding does not justify raising it, so P3 stands.

CVE-2021-23017 (CVSS 7.7, not KEV-listed) affects the exact nginx/1.18.0 version (ev-enr-0046, ev-ti-0009) on a medium-importance host. It is exploitable only by an attacker who can forge DNS responses, so the P3 baseline fits.

The default nginx page (ev-enr-0050) is served by an exact, known-vulnerable nginx/1.18.0 (ev-enr-0046). The host looks forgotten and also lacks HSTS and CSP (ev-enr-0047, ev-enr-0048). These signals support P3, but there is no confirmed exploit path or KEV listing that would justify P2.

nginx 1.18.0 (exact version, ev-enr-0013) matches CVE-2021-23017 (CVSS 7.7, not KEV-listed, ev-ti-0001), but the host is a low-importance marketing site and the flaw requires forging DNS responses to the resolver, so there is no context to move the rubric baseline up or down.

CVSS 7.7 nginx resolver issue is not KEV-listed, and the host (ev-enr-0054) is a low-importance redirect-only host. The baseline P3 already reflects this. The CVE requires forged DNS responses and the resolver may not be in use, so there is no basis to move it up or down.
The missing HSTS header (ev-enr-0047) is a low-severity hardening gap on a medium-importance host that serves HTTPS. P4 is appropriate.
Missing HSTS on a low-importance redirect-only host (ev-enr-0056) is minor. P4 is already the lowest level, so no adjustment applies.

# External Attack Surface Report: demo-corp.example

Scan date: 2026-11-02 · Hosts discovered: 10 · Live hosts: 9
P1: 5 · P2: 2 · P3: 10 · P4: 2

## Executive summary

We found 10 hosts for demo-corp.example, and 9 are live [F-0001]. Five issues need urgent action (P1) and two more are high priority (P2). The biggest risk is that administrative systems, including the admin panel and the Jenkins build server, are open to the internet [F-0001][F-0005]. The Jenkins server runs software with a critical flaw that attackers are known to exploit in real attacks, letting them read files without logging in [F-0004]. A file-sharing server also runs outdated software with two actively exploited flaws [F-0008][F-0009]. The VPN portal is also exposed to the internet [F-0013]. The remaining findings are lower priority hardening items.

## Top recommendations

1. Patch or upgrade Jenkins on jenkins.demo-corp.example beyond 2.441 (CVE-2024-23897, actively exploited), and restrict access to the Jenkins interface to a VPN or allow-listed IPs rather than the open internet.
2. Upgrade Apache HTTP Server 2.4.49 on legacy-files.demo-corp.example to a current patched release to fix CVE-2021-41773 and CVE-2021-42013, both actively exploited. Also update OpenSSL 1.1.1k on the same host (CVE-2021-3711).
3. Remove admin.demo-corp.example from public internet access, or place it behind VPN or IP allow-listing with strong authentication.
4. Review exposure of vpn.demo-corp.example and confirm the exact GlobalProtect version is fully patched, since the version could not be verified.
5. Take staging-api.demo-corp.example off the internet or enable HTTPS and access controls. Decommission or patch the default nginx page on web2.demo-corp.example, and upgrade nginx 1.18.0 where it is found.
